title: Modularize GPU pools, immutable IAM roles, and peered bastion module with state importer tooling
author: Maya Chen
commits: mod(gpu-pool): introduce scoped-gpu-pool module with nodeAffinity and taint mapping
feat(iam): add immutable role module and sticky role bindings for GPU pools
chore(bastion): new peered-bastion module with optional host-restrictions
tools(importer): add tfstate-importer script and README for per-tenant state slicing
test: add integration tests for importer and role reconciliation
description: Context: Private installs require stricter boundaries between tenant GPU pools, stable IAM role bindings, and a hardened bastion for maintenance. This PR splits responsibilities into three small modules (gpu-pool, iam-immutable-roles, peered-bastion) and adds a lightweight tfstate importer to migrate existing monolithic state into per-tenant slices. Motivation: reduce blast radius when modifying pool scheduling labels, make IAM role upgrades non-destructive for bound resources, and simplify network egress controls via an optional peered bastion. Changes: 1) modules/gpu-pool: new module that exposes nodeAffinity, taints, autoscalerProfile, and a short-lived lease label so autoscaler/tenant leases can be reconciled without rewriting state; 2) modules/iam: immutable-role module that provisions roles with stable logical IDs and a binding resource that is deliberately additive-only (prevents accidental role replacement during plan/apply); 3) modules/bastion: peered-bastion module that supports VPC peering or VPN attachment for private installs and optional host allowlist via security groups; 4) scripts/tfstate-importer: bash helper that automates terraform import into new per-tenant backends and emits an audit log for each import operation; 5) examples and integration tests for the importer and IAM reconciliation. Migration plan checklist: [x] smoke import for one test tenant; [x] validate plan shows only additions for IAM bindings; [x] run integration tests in staging; [x] run a controlled rollout across two clusters; [ ] monitor cost/latency for 48h after migration. Related: Linear ENG-9876 (private install hardening), SUP-821 (customer tenant migration). Notes: importer is intentionally idempotent but requires operator approval for each tenant; the immutable-role design means role updates create new roles side-by-side and a short TTL garbage collector is provided in the module to clean orphaned role ARNs after manual verification. Documentation: scripts/tfstate-importer/README.md contains step-by-step migration commands and a dry-run mode. Why this is different: instead of moving tfstate boundaries wholesale, we introduce a focused importer workflow plus additive IAM bindings to minimize disruption during upgrades and to keep GPU pool changes localized.
reviews: Jared Park: Reviewed the importer script, suggested stricter validation for backend configs - resolved by adding a backend checksum and explicit confirmation prompt.
Sven Olsson: Asked about rollback semantics if import partially succeeds - added a --dry-run and a rollback helper that restores state from a snapshot; confirmed in tests.
Priya Kapoor: Security review: requested host-restriction option on bastion and an allowlist for admin CIDRs - added security_group_allowed_cidrs variable and updated README.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed comments and pushed follow-ups; ran live migration on staging cluster and reported no destructive IAM diffs.
release_notes: Introduce modular GPU pool module with tenant-scoped labels and taint mapping
Add immutable IAM role module to avoid destructive role replacements during upgrades
Introduce peered bastion module with host allowlist for private installs
Add tfstate-importer tooling and integration tests to migrate monolithic state to per-tenant backends
deployment_notes: Step 1: Run scripts/tfstate-importer/tenant_import.sh --dry-run for target tenant and review generated audit log
Step 2: Apply gpu-pool and iam modules in staging using per-tenant backend and confirm 'plan' shows only additions
Step 3: Promote to prod with small batch of tenants and monitor IAM/serving logs for 1 hour
Rollback: If imports fail mid-way, use terraform state pull from snapshot and scripts/tfstate-importer/rollback_snapshot.sh to restore state before repeating import
files_changed_snippet: modules/iam/roles.tf: resource "aws_iam_role" "gpu_node_role" { name = local.role_name assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document/node_assume.json # immutable name via local.role_name } // binding is a separate resource that uses for_each over var.bindings to be additive-only
note: This PR intentionally keeps changes small per module and provides operator tooling to prevent large single-shot tfstate surgeries; follow-up work planned: garbage collector for orphaned IAM roles and a telemetry signal in console to show imported tenants.
